title: Why I Started Writing Online
content:
There's something deeply vulnerable about putting your thoughts on the internet.

For a long time, I kept journals — private, password-locked, hidden. But one day I realised that the ideas I was hoarding were not mine to keep. They were borrowed from conversations, books, and quiet moments of clarity that deserved to be shared.

So I started writing publicly. Not for an audience, at first. Just for the discipline of finishing a thought.

And something interesting happened: writing for others forced me to think more clearly. You can ramble in a private journal. But when someone else might read it, you owe them the courtesy of coherence.

That's why I'm here. Writing to think. Thinking to write.
excerpt: There's something deeply vulnerable about putting your thoughts on the internet. For a long time, I kept journals — private, hidden. Then one day I decided to share.

title: On Slow Mornings and Intentional Living
content:
I used to wake up and immediately reach for my phone.

The news, the notifications, the emails — all of it rushing in before I had even decided what kind of day I wanted to have. It felt productive. It wasn't.

Slow mornings changed everything for me. An hour before the world demands anything. Tea, not coffee. A book or a notebook. Silence that isn't empty but full.

Intentional living doesn't mean doing less. It means doing things with attention. It means choosing where your energy goes before the day chooses for you.
excerpt: I used to wake up and immediately reach for my phone. Slow mornings changed everything — an hour of quiet before the world demands anything.
